seoTitle: How to Get Semrush Pro for Free the Legit Way (2026)
metaDescription: The official, safe way to try Semrush Pro+ for free in 2026: which of Semrush's four plans actually offer a trial, what canceling really requires, and where cracked "free" versions go wrong.
intro:
Semrush Pro+ packs in keyword research, competitor analysis, backlink data, and site audits, but the price tag is a real barrier if you just want to test it first. The legitimate path is a free trial that requires a card up front and bills automatically once it ends. That's fine, as long as you know exactly when the charge lands and what canceling actually involves.

This guide covers finding the trial on Semrush's own pricing page, which of its four plans offer one, and how to walk away without being charged.
prerequisites: A credit or debit card — Semrush requires one to start the trial even though you won't be charged if you cancel in time
A Semrush account, created during signup if you don't already have one
costNote: The trial itself is free for 7 days. After that, Semrush bills the plan's regular rate automatically: Pro+ runs about $248/month on annual billing, more if billed monthly. Semrush's one-time, 7-day money-back guarantee only covers a first annual purchase made by card directly on semrush.com. A trial defaults into month-to-month billing, and month-to-month plans are non-refundable, so missing the cancellation deadline means the charge is final.

steps.heading: Search for Semrush and go to the official site
steps.body: Search for "semrush" instead of clicking a random ad or a third-party "free Semrush" result. The organic listing for semrush.com is what you want, with Google's quick links to Pricing and the Free Keyword Tool usually sitting just beneath it. Staying on the official domain is the best protection against the cracked-tool scams that circulate around expensive SEO software; more on those at the end of this guide.

image.caption: A Google search for Semrush, with Pricing and Free Keyword Tool listed as direct links under the official result.

steps.heading: Compare the four plans and pick Pro+
steps.body:
Semrush's pricing page currently lists four tiers side by side: SEO, Starter, Pro+, and Advanced. SEO, Starter, and Pro+ each carry a "Try for free" button; Advanced is subscribe-only, sold as a direct purchase or a custom plan with no trial attached.

Pro+ is the tier most people mean when they say "Semrush Pro." On top of everything in Starter, it adds historical SEO data, content optimization tools, keyword-cannibalization analysis, multi-location tracking, and roughly triple the sites and keywords you can monitor. Read the feature list on the pricing page before signing up so you know what you're testing.

image.caption: Semrush's pricing page comparing its plans, with a "Try for free" button under the Pro+ column.

steps.heading: Start the trial and enter payment details
steps.body: Clicking "Try for free" under Pro+ leads to a subscription page that states its terms plainly: a 7-day free trial, a listed next-charge date, and required card fields. This is a real subscription that activates automatically unless you cancel first. Semrush shows the exact next-charge date on this screen, so there's no ambiguity about the deadline.

steps.heading: Read exactly how the trial works
steps.body: The signup screen includes a "How your free trial works" breakdown: instant access today, a full week to explore the platform, and automatic billing at the full plan cost on day 7 unless you cancel. There's also a direct link to the cancellation policy on this same page. Open it once now, since the cancellation process has a couple of steps worth knowing before you're up against the deadline.

image.caption: The trial signup screen showing the day-by-day "How your free trial works" timeline and a link to the cancellation policy.

steps.heading: Use the trial to test Pro+ features
steps.body: Once you're in, spend the week on the tools you'd actually pay for: competitor keyword gaps, backlink audits, and the Site Audit tool are what most clearly separate Pro+ from Semrush's free tools. Testing against a real project or domain, not a throwaway search, is what tells you whether the paid plan earns its cost once the trial ends.

image.caption: The logged-in Semrush dashboard, ready to run a project through the tools included in the trial.

steps.heading: Cancel correctly before the charge date
steps.body:
Log in and submit a cancellation request through the form linked from your account or from the signup screen. Semrush then emails a confirmation link that must be clicked within 24 hours, and the cancellation itself can take up to 3 business days to process. Do this a few days before the charge date shown at signup, not the night before; a cancellation still waiting on that email click when billing runs will not stop the charge.

If all of this sounds like more hassle than it's worth, that's a reason to skip the trial rather than to look for a cracked or third-party "free" version. Those aren't official, don't reliably work, and are a common vector for credential theft or malware.

troubleshooting.problem: I canceled but got charged anyway
troubleshooting.cause: Semrush cancellation isn't instant. It requires submitting the form while logged in, then clicking a confirmation link emailed within 24 hours, and the whole process can take up to 3 business days.
troubleshooting.fix: Cancel several days before the listed charge date, not the day before, and check your inbox immediately for the confirmation email.

troubleshooting.problem: I want a refund for the charge after the trial converted
troubleshooting.cause: Semrush's money-back guarantee applies only to a first annual subscription bought by card on semrush.com. A trial defaults into month-to-month billing, which is non-refundable.
troubleshooting.fix: If there's a real chance you'll keep the subscription, switch to annual billing before the trial ends to stay eligible for the guarantee. Otherwise treat the trial's end date as final.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no "Try for free" button under the Advanced plan
troubleshooting.cause: Semrush sells Advanced by direct subscription or a custom quote only. The trial is limited to the SEO, Starter, and Pro+ tiers.
troubleshooting.fix: Trial one of those three tiers instead, or contact Semrush sales for an Advanced demo.

faq.question: Does Semrush actually offer a free trial in 2026?
faq.answer: Yes. Semrush's SEO, Starter, and Pro+ plans each show a 7-day "Try for free" option on the official pricing page. The Advanced plan does not; it's subscribe-only.

faq.question: Will I be charged automatically after the trial?
faq.answer: Yes. The trial requires a card upfront and bills the plan's full price on day 7 unless you cancel before then.

faq.question: Are 'free Semrush Pro' tools from other websites safe?
faq.answer: No. Cracked or third-party 'free' versions aren't official, generally don't work, and can expose your data or device to malware.

faq.question: How far ahead should I cancel to be safe?
faq.answer: A few days before the charge date. Cancellation needs a confirmation link clicked within 24 hours and can take up to 3 business days to finish processing, so canceling the night before can be too late.

faq.question: Can I get my money back if I forget to cancel in time?
faq.answer: Only if you were on an annual plan bought directly by card on semrush.com, and only within Semrush's one-time 7-day guarantee. Month-to-month charges, which is what a trial becomes by default, are non-refundable.
